1.title: HCP Terraform
1.text: Welcome to Module sixteen: H C P Terraform. It covers the exam area eight. H C P Terraform. Each part of this module comes from the study notes of the same name, so you can read the notes after you watch.

1.text: By the end of this module you will be able to do five things. eight A Use H C P Terraform to create infrastructure. eight B Describe H C P Terraform collaboration and governance features. eight C Describe how to organize and use H C P Terraform workspaces and projects. eight D Configure and use H C P Terraform integration. 1.title: Where This Fits in the Exam
1.text: Here is where this module sits in the exam. Exam area: eight. H C P Terraform. Exam format: a one-hour online-proctored multiple-choice exam on Terraform one point one two. Validated against: the official Terraform Associate version oh oh four exam objectives.

1.title: What HCP Terraform is
1.text: What H C P Terraform is. H C P Terraform is Hashi Corp's managed service for running Terraform in a team. It adds remote state, remote runs, collaboration and governance to the Community edition of Terraform. (Terraform Enterprise is the self-hosted version.).

1.title: What HCP Terraform is, continued
1.text: What H C P Terraform is. The figure shows this: Organization contains projects, projects contain workspaces, each workspace has state, variables and runs.

1.title: What HCP Terraform is, continued
1.text: What H C P Terraform is. Remote state. Stored, versioned, encrypted and locked by the service. Remote operations. Plan and apply run on H C P Terraform, not on your laptop. Collaboration. Shared workspaces, run history, comments, teams. Governance. Policy enforcement, cost estimation, private registry, access control. Security. Sensitive variables, dynamic credentials.

1.title: Organizations, projects and workspaces
1.text: Organizations, projects and workspaces. Organization. The top level of an account: teams, settings and billing. Project. A group of workspaces (for example per team or product); permissions and variable sets can be applied to a project. Workspace. One unit of infrastructure: its own configuration, state, variables, run history and permissions. H C P Terraform workspaces differ from C L I workspaces. A C L I workspace is another state file in the same working directory and backend. An H C P Terraform workspace is a full environment with its own variables, permissions and runs. Exam tip: Organization to project to workspace. A workspace holds state, variables and runs. Projects organize workspaces and share access rules.

1.title: Workflows to create infrastructure
1.text: Workflows to create infrastructure. Version control (V C S)-driven. Connect a repository; a commit or merge starts a run; pull requests start speculative plans. C L I-driven. Use the terraform C L I locally; plan and apply run remotely in a workspace. A P I-driven. Call the H C P Terraform A P I from other tools (for example a pipeline). A run has stages: plan, optional policy checks and cost estimate, then apply (after approval, or automatically if auto-apply is on). A speculative plan only shows changes and cannot be applied.

1.title: Integration: the cloud block and login
1.text: Integration: the cloud block and login. The example is on the screen; read it line by line when you study.

1.title: Integration: the cloud block and login, continued
1.text: Integration: the cloud block and login. Authenticate. terraform login stores an A P I token on your machine. Connect. The cloud block names the organization and workspace (or tags or a project). Initialize. terraform init; it can migrate existing local state into the workspace. Run. terraform plan and terraform apply run remotely and stream the output to your terminal. Execution mode. Remote (on H C P Terraform), local (on your machine, state in H C P Terraform) or agent (your own runners). Exam tip: terraform login gets the token; the cloud block selects the workspace. A remote run still prints its output in your terminal.

1.title: Collaboration and governance features
1.text: Collaboration and governance features. Teams and permissions. Role-based access to organizations, projects and workspaces (read, plan, write, admin). Variable sets. Reusable sets of variables applied to many workspaces or projects; sensitive values are write-only. Run triggers. Start a run in one workspace when another applies successfully. Policy enforcement. Sentinel or Open Policy Agent (O P A) policies check every run; levels such as advisory and mandatory. Cost estimation. Estimates the monthly cost of a plan.

1.title: Collaboration and governance features, continued
1.text: Collaboration and governance features. Private registry. Your own private modules and providers. Drift detection. Health assessments that check regularly for drift and run checks. Dynamic provider credentials. Short-lived credentials through workload identity, instead of stored keys. Explorer and change requests. See and track workspaces and their health across the organization. Exam tip: Variable sets share variables, run triggers chain workspaces, policies (Sentinel or O P A) enforce rules, the private registry shares modules.

1.title: Practice Question 1
1.text: Question one. A team wants plan and apply to run on a managed service and the state to be stored and locked there. What should it use? The four options are on the screen. The answer is D: H C P Terraform. H C P Terraform provides remote operations, and stores, versions and locks the state.

1.title: Practice Question 2
1.text: Question two. What is a project in H C P Terraform? The four options are on the screen. The answer is C: A group of workspaces with shared access settings. Projects organize workspaces and let teams apply permissions and variable sets to many of them.

1.title: Practice Question 3
1.text: Question three. Which command stores an A P I token so the C L I can talk to H C P Terraform? The four options are on the screen. The answer is B: terraform login. terraform login obtains and stores the A P I token used to authenticate.

1.title: Practice Question 4
1.text: Question four. Which block connects a configuration to an H C P Terraform workspace? The four options are on the screen. The answer is A: The cloud block. The cloud block names the organization and workspace.

1.title: Practice Question 5
1.text: Question five. An organization wants to apply the same set of cloud credentials variables to many workspaces. What should it use? The four options are on the screen. The answer is B: A variable set. Variable sets are reusable groups of variables applied to many workspaces or projects.

1.title: Practice Question 6
1.text: Question six. Which feature starts a run in a second workspace after the first workspace applies successfully? The four options are on the screen. The answer is A: A run trigger. Run triggers chain workspaces so that one run starts after another succeeds.

1.title: Recall Check 1
1.text: Recall check one. Say each answer out loud before you listen to mine. Question one. What does a workspace hold in H C P Terraform? Answer: Configuration, state, variables, run history and permissions. Question two. What groups workspaces? Answer: A project. Question three. Which command authenticates the C L I? Answer: terraform login.

1.title: Recall Check 2
1.text: Recall check two. Say each answer out loud before you listen to mine. Question four. Name two policy frameworks. Answer: Sentinel and Open Policy Agent. Question five. What is a speculative plan? Answer: A plan that shows changes and cannot be applied. Question six. What is Terraform Enterprise? Answer: The self-hosted version of H C P Terraform.

1.title: Module Recap
1.text: Here is the recap. H C P Terraform: managed service: remote state, remote runs, collaboration, governance. Hierarchy: organization, project, workspace (state, variables, runs). Workflows: V C S-driven, C L I-driven, A P I-driven. Integration: cloud block, terraform login, init migrates state, remote execution. Features: teams, variable sets, run triggers, Sentinel and O P A, cost estimation, private registry, drift detection, dynamic credentials.
